source.title: MoSECroT: Model Stitching with Static Word Embeddings for Crosslingual Zero-shot Transfer
source.authors: Haotian Ye; Yihong Liu; Chunlan Ma; Hinrich Schütze

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether mapped representations can be used across models by evaluating zero-shot transfer after swapping in mapped target-language embeddings. This is a task-performance test of interchangeability, not a direct measurement of representation similarity.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream macro-F1 results for relative-representation (RR) embedding mapping and stitching, plus results under different anchor-set sizes. Table 3 varies the number of closest anchors to identify a setting; those values are omitted because they are used to choose a hyperparameter. Baseline model scores are not rows because they do not measure the mapped representations or the stitching operation.
record.test_reason: The paper builds a stitching method on the assumed similarity of representations (citing Kornblith, Vulić, Moschella) and reports only downstream macro-F1 of its own method against other transfer methods (LR, mBERT, least-squares projection). It never compares a stitched model with an unstitched reference such as English-on-English or a native target model. So no row shows how much is lost by mapping one model's representations onto another's. The mapping also links embeddings of different languages through translation anchors, not the same inputs across models. This is a method-performance result, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors present a negative result: RR-based stitching beats the naive LS projection and mBERT on languages mBERT does not cover, but it fails against strong baselines. It falls short of mBERT on high-resource languages and of target-language LR on Taxi1500. Improvements are modest. They attribute this to noisy anchors and lexica, poor PanLex translation quality, and the reinitialized embedding space.
record.recipe_differences: Uses relative representations and embedding-layer swapping for crosslingual transfer, then evaluates downstream classification; it does not reproduce a direct cross-model representation-similarity measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The results vary with the RR weighting scheme (standard, softmax, sparsemax), target language and dataset. Appendix B reports different scores for different anchor-set sizes; the paper also states that removing stop words did not improve results.

fits_no_version.finding: Swapping English BERT's embedding layer for fastText target-language embeddings aligned via relative representations gives weak zero-shot transfer. Amazon macro F1 is 0.24-0.57, below mBERT on de/es/zh (0.51-0.65). On Taxi1500, RRs beat mBERT on 5 unseen low-resource languages by +0.01 to +0.12, but stay well below a target-language LR classifier (e.g. mt 0.15 vs 0.38). A least-squares linear projection baseline does worse still (0.06-0.46).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aligning static word embeddings of a target language to a monolingual PLM's input embeddings, via anchor-based relative representations or linear projection, supports only weak crosslingual zero-shot stitching.

record.peer_reviewed: First Workshop on Insights from Negative Results in NLP
record.problems: Only one model architecture is tested; only text-classification tasks are evaluated. The central outcome is downstream task performance, not a direct measure of mapped-representation similarity or mapping loss. Table 2 reports averages over five runs but no variability estimate.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix A, Table 3 is omitted because its anchor-count sweep is used to identify the top-k setting. Baseline-model results in Tables 1 and 2 are omitted because they do not measure the RR-mapped representations or stitching operation.

untested.parts: No direct measure of mapping loss or representation similarity. No stitching at intermediate layers. No comparison of same-input representations across models. Only one source model (bert-base-cased), with fastText as the target.
No analysis of the degree of alignment or its causes.

missing.what: Least-squares linear projection (LS) stitching scores, relevant to how well a simple linear map works in this setting. The record excludes them as baselines.
missing.versions: none (would bear on V4 only if a no-mapping reference existed)

record.verdict_notes: Workshop on negative results. One source model, classification only, no variance reported despite five seeds on Taxi1500. The RR weighting scheme (standard, softmax, sparsemax) changes scores substantially, e.g. zh Taxi1500 0.28 vs 0.13. Even if treated as V4 evidence, the lack of a no-mapping reference prevents any judgement about 'little loss'.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability scaling, and no comparison of independently trained models across architectures, objectives, data, or modalities.
No vision-language models or paired images and captions.
No comparison of networks trained from different initializations or analysis of shared features or subspaces.

Tests RR-based embedding mapping and embedding-layer swapping for crosslingual classification only. It does not test linear maps, stitching at other layers, relative representations without paired anchors, or representation loss directly.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are examined.
Varies anchor settings, but does not measure convergence under alternative similarity metrics or test out-of-distribution inputs.
Does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment.

rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned on English data; training method not stated
rows.operation_detail: Zero-shot classification after replacing the source embedding layer with RR-mapped target-language embeddings.
rows.note: The paper reports the result as zero-shot performance; it does not directly measure representation similarity or loss from mapping.
rows.check: These are the study's own method (RR stitching) scored by macro F1 and compared only with other transfer methods. reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: RR-mapped embedding swaps on the tested classification datasets and target languages
reader_labels.reason: The mapping supports some zero-shot transfer, but the paper reports only modest gains overall, no RR setting exceeding mBERT on the high-resource Amazon languages, and very weak results for some Taxi1500 languages; these task scores do not establish little representation loss directly (R1-R39).
